tasks.text: Download Cambridge IELTS 15–20 from [ieltsworldly.com](https://www.ieltsworldly.com/cambridge-ielts-19-pdf/)
Watch [IELTS Liz "IELTS Exam Format"](https://www.youtube.com/@ieltsliz) (20 min) — understand the test structure

Read official Band 7 descriptors from [ielts.org](https://ielts.org/take-a-test/preparation-resources) — read per-criterion: Speaking (FC/LR/GRA/P), Writing Task 1 (TA/CC/LR/GRA), Task 2 (TR/CC/LR/GRA)

**TAKE FULL MOCK TEST #1** using [ieltstestsimulation.com](https://www.ieltstestsimulation.com/) (Cambridge 15 Test 1, timed, 2h45min) or [ieltsonlinetests.com](https://ieltsonlinetests.com/ielts-exam-library)

Score yourself (Listening/Reading = raw count; Writing = assess per criterion (TA/CC/LR/GRA for Task 1, TR/CC/LR/GRA for Task 2); Speaking = per criterion (FC/LR/GRA/P); note your **ceiling criterion** (lowest score))
**Log results in PrepSprint** `+ Add test result` → fill test name, type, score, notes
Identify your weakest section → this gets 50% of study time going forward
Set up Anki with an IELTS vocabulary deck from [ankiweb.net](https://apps.ankiweb.net/)

PrepSprint now has a built-in **Error Log** — after each entry review, expand the card and log mistakes using **examiner categories**: Speaking = FC/LR/GRA/P, Writing Task 1 = TA/CC/LR/GRA, Writing Task 2 = TR/CC/LR/GRA and note the fix

Skim the [Speaking examiner reference](file://examiner-agent/speaking-examiner-agent.md) (5min) and [Writing examiner reference](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md) (5min) — understand what examiners actually measure per criterion
REVIEW mock test in detail — categorize EVERY wrong answer:
Watch [IELTS Liz "Writing Task 2 Introduction Formula"](https://www.youtube.com/@ieltsliz) on YouTube
Write 1 Task 2 essay (timed 40min) — use Liz's formula; log in **PrepSprint**
Run essay through [ChatGPT](https://chat.openai.com/) with: 'Score this Task 2 essay by criterion (TR/CC/LR/GRA). Give a band per criterion and specific recommendations for each.'
Watch [IELTS Simon "Reading: True/False/Not Given"](https://www.youtube.com/@Ieltssimon) strategy video
Practice 1 Reading passage (timed 20min) from [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) Cambridge 15 Test 2
Start daily [BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) habit (20min)
Use **PrepSprint Focus Timer** for all timed sections — build the habit
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (20min) — listen + read transcript
1 full Listening test on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (Cambridge 15 Test 2, 30min) — use **PrepSprint Focus Timer**
Review every wrong answer in Listening — add to the entry's **Error Log** (category + what went wrong + fix)
Watch [Fastrack IELTS "Top 10 Listening Mistakes"](https://www.youtube.com/@FastrackIELTS) video
Anki vocabulary: 15 new words + review

Speaking Part 1 practice — record 5 answers. Self-evaluate on Pronunciation: (1) **stress-timing** — do you sound syllable-timed (robotic) or stress-timed (natural)? (2) **chunking** — do you pause mid-phrase or at syntactic boundaries? (3) **intonation** — flat or varied pitch? See [Pronunciation taxonomy](file://examiner-agent/speaking-examiner-agent.md#L142-L222)
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (20min)
Reading: 2 passages timed (20min each = 40min) from [ieltstestsimulation.com](https://www.ieltstestsimulation.com/) Cambridge 15
REVIEW both passages — add wrong answers to the entry's **Error Log**
Watch [IELTS Advantage "Reading: Matching Headings Strategy"](https://www.youtube.com/@Ieltsadvantage)
Anki: 15 new words

Speaking: Record Part 2 cue card (2min). Evaluate: FC (hesitation count), P (stress-timing/chunking). Also note which [GRA tier](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L245-L252) your spoken grammar is at: Tier 1 (basic), Tier 2 (lower complex), or Tier 3 (mid complex)
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
WRITING INTENSIVE: Write 1 Task 1 + 1 Task 2. After feedback, categorise EVERY error by criterion (TA/TR, CC, LR, GRA) — check which criterion has the most errors
Run both through [engnovate.com](https://engnovate.com/) for AI feedback
**Log both in PrepSentry** with scores and paste the AI feedback in notes
Add feedback points to "Writing Fix List" in **PrepSprint Notebook** — organise by criterion (TA/TR, CC, LR, GRA) so you can spot patterns
Speaking: Part 3 practice — 3 questions. After recording, self-evaluate: FC (language-related hesitation?), LR (paraphrase success? any less common vocab?), GRA (errors in complex structures?)
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
FULL LISTENING TEST on [ieltsonlinetests.com](https://ieltsonlinetests.com/ielts-exam-library) (Cambridge 15 Test 3, 30min) — timed
REVIEW with audio script — underline missed answers
Watch [E2 IELTS "Listening: Map Labelling & Multiple Choice"](https://www.youtube.com/@E2IELTS)
Reading: 1 full test (60min) — [ieltstestsimulation.com](https://www.ieltstestsimulation.com/) Cambridge 16 Test 1
**Log tests in PrepSprint** — add errors to each entry's **Error Log**
Anki: review + 15 new words
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)

WRITING: Rewrite 1 essay from Day 5 — specifically replace mechanical linkers (firstly/secondly/moreover) with **reference chains** (this/these/such + noun) and **lexical chains** (synonyms for core topic)
Compare before/after — note what changed in **PrepSprint Notebook**
Speaking: Join free Telegram speaking groups (search "IELTS Speaking Practice" in Telegram) for 20min live practice
Watch [IELTS Simon "Writing Task 1: How to Write an Overview"](https://www.youtube.com/@Ieltssimon)
Anki review

Study the [CC device taxonomy](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L284-L318) — identify which of the 5 device types you currently use and which you avoid. Write 1 paragraph using 3+ types
**FULL MOCK TEST #2** on [ieltsonlinetests.com](https://ieltsonlinetests.com/ielts-exam-library) (Cambridge 16 Test 2, timed, 2h45min)
30min break
REVIEW ENTIRE TEST (2–3 hours):
**Log everything in PrepSprint** — use per-type entry cards
Update **Error Log** for each section using examiner categories → identify TOP 3 error patterns AND note your **ceiling criterion** per skill (the weakest criterion determines the overall band)
Watch YouTube on your #1 error pattern from the channels above
Create a "One-Page Cheat Sheet" in **PrepSprint Notebook** with your personal error patterns **grouped by criterion** (TA/TR, CC, LR, GRA, FC, P) + a specific fix for each
WEAK AREA DRILL — spend 3 hours on your lowest-scoring section
STRONG SECTION MAINTENANCE (1 hour):
Speaking: Record full Speaking test (Parts 1+2+3, 15min) — use [ieltsup.com speaking simulator](https://ielts-up.com/ielts-speaking-simulator.html)

Criterion-by-criterion review: FC (hesitation count, coherence), LR (vocab range, paraphrase quality), GRA (error rate in complex structures vs simple), P (stress-timing, chunking, intonation) — note which criterion is your **ceiling**
**Log all in PrepSprint**
Plan next week's focus based on error patterns

Pronunciation drill (15min): Practice **stress-timing** with 5 sentences from [BBC Learning English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/) — mark stressed syllables (louder/longer), reduce unstressed ones. Record and compare. This single feature separates Band 6 from Band 7 in Pronunciation
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
FULL LISTENING TEST on [ieltsonlinetests.com](https://ieltsonlinetests.com/ielts-exam-library) (Cambridge 16 Test 3, 30min) — focus on Section 4
REVIEW Section 4 specifically — practice with [TED Talks](https://www.ted.com/talks) at 1.25x speed
Reading: 1 full test (60min) on [ieltstestsimulation.com](https://www.ieltstestsimulation.com/) — focus on Passage 3 timing (allow 25min)
**Log in PrepSprint** — add errors to the entry's **Error Log**
Anki: 15 new words + review all
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
WRITING: Write 1 Task 2 essay on a HARD topic from [ieltsliz.com 2026 topics](https://ieltsliz.com/ielts-essay-topics-for-2026/)
AI feedback via [engnovate.com](https://engnovate.com/) → note recurring grammar errors

Study 1 grammar **tier** from the [4-tier hierarchy](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L245-L252) — pick the tier matching your target band (Tier 3 for Band 7, Tier 4 for Band 8). Write 5 sentences using those structures
Speaking: Part 2 practice — 3 different cue cards from [ieltsliz.com](https://ieltsliz.com/), record all
Anki: review + 15 new collocations

⚠️ Read [template penalty rules](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L551-L553) — examiners in 2026 penalise memorised language (TR capped at Band 4). Learn to detect and avoid canned phrases in your own writing
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
LISTENING FOCUS: Section 4 only from 3 different tests on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (Cambridge 16 Test 4, Cambridge 17 Tests 1–2)
Reading FOCUS: Matching Headings questions only (20 questions from 2 passages)
Watch [Fastrack IELTS "True/False/Not Given — The Complete Guide"](https://www.youtube.com/@FastrackIELTS)
Review **Error Log** across all entries (10min) — for Speaking/Writing errors, group by criterion (FC/CC/LR/GRA/P/TA/TR). If one criterion dominates, that's your **score ceiling** and needs focus
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
WRITING: Write 1 Task 1 (graph/chart) + 1 Task 2 from [ielts-up.com](https://ielts-up.com/writing/ielts-writing-practice.html)
STUDY: 5 Band 9 sample essays — but **paraphrase** every phrase you extract into your own words (examiners penalise memorised chunks in 2026). Add paraphrased versions to Anki, not verbatim
Speaking: Part 1 — 10 questions from [ieltstestsimulation.com](https://www.ieltstestsimulation.com/wb-cnt/speaking/overview/), give 3+ sentence answers each
Add new phrases to Anki
Read 1 article from [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/international) (science/tech section)
CC drill (10min): Write **3 reference chains** on a topic (e.g., environment). Chain 3 sentences: 'This measure... Such policies... These approaches...' — no overt linkers needed
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
LIGHT REVIEW DAY:
1 Listening test on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (Cambridge 17 Test 1, 30min) — aim for 30+/40
1 Reading test on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (Cambridge 17 Test 1, 60min) — aim for 30+/40
Speaking: Telegram voice chat (20min)
Prepare mentally for tomorrow's mock
**FULL MOCK TEST #3** on [ieltstestsimulation.com](https://www.ieltstestsimulation.com/) (Cambridge 17 Test 2, timed, 2h45min)
30min break
COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW (3 hours):
**Log all in PrepSprint** — compare with Stats page
Create "Final 10-Day Strategy": identify your **ceiling criterion** per section (the weakest criterion determines the overall band). Prioritise that criterion over all others
Watch 1 video on weakest area from YouTube channels above
TARGETED WEAK AREA (3 hours):
STRONG AREA MAINTENANCE (1.5 hours): quick test in best section

REVIEW common mistakes from research — group by examiner criterion. If all errors cluster in one criterion, that's your **score ceiling**. If spread across multiple, pick the most impactful one to fix
Anki: massive review session (all cards)

CC deep work (20min): Take 1 of your old essays. Replace every overt linker (firstly/secondly/moreover/however) with **referencing** (this/these/such + noun) + **lexical cohesion** (synonyms). Check the [CC taxonomy](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L284-L318) for your target band
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
Listening: Cambridge 17 Test 3 on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (30min, timed)
Review — spelling mistakes: write out every misspelled word 5 times
Reading: Cambridge 17 Test 3 Passage 1+2 on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (40min timed)
Add new vocab to Anki

Speaking: Record Part 2 + Part 3. Self-evaluate GRA: count total sentences, count complex sentences, count errors in complex vs simple. Aim for 2–3 errors/100 words (Band 7) not 4–6 (Band 6). See [error rate table](file://examiner-agent/speaking-examiner-agent.md#L240-L247)

Connected speech drill (10min): Practice natural linking (turn_it_off, next_week→neksweek, don't_you→donchu). Record yourself reading 3 BBC transcript sentences, then compare with the original. Connected speech is a Band 8+ Pronunciation differentiator. See [features](file://examiner-agent/speaking-examiner-agent.md#L176-L179)
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
WRITING: Task 2 only — write 1 Opinion essay from [ieltsliz.com 2026 topics](https://ieltsliz.com/ielts-essay-topics-for-2026/) (timed 40min)
AI feedback via [ielts-gpt.com](https://ielts-gpt.com/) → check Task Response

STUDY: 3 Band 9 essays from [ieltsliz.com](https://ieltsliz.com/) — highlight structure **and** map their CC devices: which of the 5 types (reference, substitution, conjunction, lexical cohesion, paragraphing) do they use? Compare with [CC taxonomy](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L284-L318)
Speaking: Part 3 deep dive — 5 questions with reasons+examples
Anki: 10 new high-level collocations

GRA upgrade drill (10min): Take 5 simple sentences from one of your old essays. Rewrite each as a **complex sentence** using relative clauses, conditionals, or passive voice. This trains Tier 2→3 progression. See [structure types by band](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L245-L262)
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
Reading: Full test on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (Cambridge 18 Test 1, 60min)
Practice 18-min per passage speed drill (Band 8 technique)
1 [TED Talk](https://www.ted.com/talks) at 1.25x speed (15min) — take notes
Review **Error Log** across all entries (10min)
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
WRITING: Task 1 + Task 2 (timed, 60min total) from [ielts-up.com](https://ielts-up.com/writing/ielts-writing-practice.html)
Spend FIRST 5 minutes PLANNING (Band 8 habit)

AI feedback via [engnovate.com](https://engnovate.com/) — specifically check CC: count unique discourse marker types (aim for 6–10 at Band 7), count overt linkers per paragraph (aim for 2–4, not 5–6), check reference chain clarity. See [CC benchmarks](file://examiner-agent/writing-examiner-agent.md#L311-L318)
Speaking: Full test recording (15min) using [ieltstestsimulation.com](https://www.ieltstestsimulation.com/wb-cnt/speaking/overview/)
Listen back — score by criterion: FC (hesitation count/min), LR (any less common vocab?), GRA (error rate in complex vs simple), P (stress-timing). Note your **ceiling criterion** for speaking
[BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min)
LIGHT DAY:
1 Listening test on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (Cambridge 18 Test 2, 30min)
1 Reading test on [ieltsolve.com](https://www.ieltsolve.com/) (Cambridge 18 Test 2, 60min) — target 32+/40
Watch [IELTS Speaking band 7+ sample](https://www.youtube.com/@IELTSbyIDP) (20min)
No new material — consolidation only
**FULL MOCK TEST #4** on [ieltsonlinetests.com](https://ieltsonlinetests.com/ielts-exam-library) (Cambridge 19 Test 1, timed, 2h45min)
30min break
EXHAUSTIVE REVIEW (3 hours): score per criterion per section. Determine your **ceiling criterion** for each skill — that's what's holding your band back
Identify 1–2 things to fix → convert to **criterion-targeted actions** (e.g., 'Fix CC: replace firstly/secondly with reference chains' or 'Fix P: practice stress-timing on 10 BBC sentences')
Prepare test day logistics:
LAST INTENSIVE SESSION:
REVIEW everything — focus on NOT repeating the same errors
Create "Test Day Checklist" in **PrepSprint Notebook**
Finalize One-Page Cheat Sheet: YOUR top 5 mistakes + fixes — **organised by criterion** (TA/TR, CC, LR, GRA, FC, P) so you can scan by skill on test day
Watch [IELTS by IDP "Test Day Tips"](https://www.youtube.com/@IELTSbyIDP) (15min)
Pack your bag. SLEEP EARLY.
**ABSOLUTELY NO HARD STUDY**
Review One-Page Cheat Sheet in **PrepSprint Notebook** (10min)
Listen to [BBC 6 Minute English](https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/english/features/6-minute-english) (15min) — relaxed
Read through Writing Fix List (10min) — note the criterion each fix targets. Remind yourself of your ceiling criterion per section
Review Speaking Part 1&2 topics from [ieltsliz.com](https://ieltsliz.com/ielts-speaking-topics-2026/) (15min)
Relax. Trust your preparation. Sleep 8+ hours.
